A.notes: Decoder change is minimal and matches the existing per-bit if-block pattern. Tests update the existing message to expect fuel level for unit 'P', add an explicit 'L' case (mask 0x1C0), and add a full-mask message (0x7FFFFFFFFF) whose values line up correctly with bits 0-38. The case where the unit field is absent is not tested. The full-mask check uses position(Checks.ATTRIBUTES), which differs from the plain position() used elsewhere in the file. It is probably valid, but it adds another style.

B.notes: Production code is essentially the same as A. It also treats an empty unit string as liters, which is a reasonable reading of 'absent' and costs nothing. Tests cover all three fuel cases: non-L unit becomes fuel level, an absent unit (mask 0x100 with only bit 8 set) stays as fuel in liters, and 'L' in the full message. The full-mask message's values line up correctly with bits 0-38, and the assertions keep the file's existing position() style.

answer.why: The two decoder changes are nearly identical and both correct. I would merge B first because its tests also cover the case where the unit field is absent, which the task names explicitly, and its test style matches the rest of the file more closely.
